label: missing-explanation-at-declaration
name: A new parameter, helper, routine, term, default or superseded document lands with no explanation a reader can use
description: What breaks: a reader of the file alone cannot learn what the thing is for. kv_hint = nullptr with no comment and a hedge word in the name (2948108341 'why is it a hint :-p'); xfer_k_entry is a unit-test-only utility that purposely forwards head_size, undocumented (3866568650, 3866590750); a 20-line device_thread routine and the TRON_POISON_BITS env var with no comment (3036997452 'I'm a fan of comments :)'); 'erased' and 'safe mode' used in a spec without definition or pointer (4095287201, 3855274893); default argument values visible only in the header (2789826297, pushed back: C++ forbids repeating them, so a comment at the definition); older specs demoted to 'no longer the authority' with no retirement plan (4095262504). Procedure: for every added signature parameter, env-var read, function over about 20 lines, header function whose callers are all under t/, and quoted or capitalized term in prose, require a definition at first use or a pointer; for defaults moved to a header suggest a comment at the definition; for 'superseded' wording ask who removes the old document and when. This is the plain-English rule 'define a term at first use' applied to code and specs.
disposition_reason: No existing check asks for documentation at a declaration; 8 rows over 6 PRs.
agent_feasibility: yes: detect undocumented new parameters, env reads, long functions, test-only header functions and first-use terms; whether a hedge word is justified needs reading the body.

members.concern: A new defaulted parameter kv_hint (a tree node pointer passed to prepare_and_launch_hw) has no comment; Wade asks for documentation, in particular why it is only a 'hint'.

detection.trigger: The diff adds a parameter to a function signature (especially with a default value such as `= nullptr`) and neither the function's leading comment nor the hunk explains it; or the parameter name carries a hedge word (hint, maybe, tmp, opt) while the body dereferences or requires it.
detection.procedure: Read the function's doc comment at HEAD for the parameter name; read the body for how the parameter is used (required dereference vs optional); grep callers for whether any passes the default; compare the name's connotation with the use.
detection.question: Does the function comment explain the new parameter, and does its name (hint) agree with whether the body treats it as optional?

members.quote: can we document `kv_hint` (e.g. why is it a 'hint' :-p)?
members.note: mcherba: 'It shouldn't be a hint, it should be required.' Author explained the edge-to-book mapping in the thread and said kv_hint will be removed after the new scheduler integration. Verified at head 429249ead6 self_attention.hpp:741-749: the signature still has `tron::node_base* kv_hint = nullptr` and the leading comment does not mention it; the explanation lives only in the GitHub thread.

members.concern: Answering another reviewer's question why xfer_k_packed_entry (the shared low-level K DMA helper) uses its head_size parameter rather than the constant HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE, Wade explains the parameter is intentional (left from supporting 64-wide gpt-oss heads), that the only production caller passes HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE, that the other callers are unit tests via xfer_k_entry which is not production-reachable, and that this should be documented.

detection.trigger: A reviewer or the diff questions a parameter that production always passes as one constant, or a header function whose only callers are under t/.
detection.procedure: Grep h/ src/ t/ for every call of the function (git grep 'xfer_k_entry(' at the reviewed commit). Classify each caller as production (h/, src/) or test (t/). Read the production caller's comment explaining the constant it passes. Read the function's doc comment and check it states (a) test-only status and (b) why the parameter is kept.
detection.question: Does the function's own doc comment say which callers are production, and why a parameter production never varies is kept?

members.quote: _that_ function is not a production-reachable function. It's basically just a test function. We really should go back and improve our documentation I suppose. Either way, this particular utility is parameterized intentionally.
members.note: Verified at 29a39ac33e: the only caller of xfer_k_entry outside its own header is t/t_hwattention.cpp:418; the production caller k_hwcacheblock::xfer passes HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE with the comment Wade pasted. Wade's history claim ('left over from evolution, after I had to start supporting gpt-oss heads that are only 64 wide') is domain knowledge an agent cannot derive from the diff. At the head 3a8544cd35 the xfer_k_entry doc comment reads 'Test-only helper: production stages K through k_hwcacheblock::set_position ... deliberately forwards the caller's head_size ... today's only caller passes head_size == HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE' (commit 'trim the slot-geometry note, document the test-only K helpers').

members.concern: Wade asks that xfer_k_entry (the one-call shuffle-and-transfer K helper) be documented as a unit-test-only utility, and that the comment also state it purposely forwards the head_size parameter instead of the constant HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE.

detection.trigger: The diff touches a header function (adds a line, renames a constant inside it) whose callers are all under t/, and whose doc comment does not say so.
detection.procedure: For every function the diff touches in h/, git grep its name across h/ src/ t/ at the reviewed commit, excluding its own definition. If every call site is under t/, read the function's doc block for the words test-only / UT-only / not production. Also compare each parameter against what the single production-like caller passes; a parameter that is always one constant needs a sentence saying why it stays a parameter.
detection.question: Would a reader of this header know, from the function's own comment, that production never calls it and why its parameter exists?

members.quote: same thing in here... this `xfer_k_entry` is a UT-only utility function. We should document that clearly, as well as the fact that it purposely uses the `head_size` parameter rather than `HW_BAKED_HEAD_SIZE`
members.note: Author replied 'Documented' on 2026-08-27. The PR body records it: 'Two helpers carry doc comments answering questions raised in review: why one keeps a head_size parameter production never varies, and that the other is test-only.' Pattern: Wade asks for a doc comment at the definition when a reviewer had to ask the question; the remedy is a comment, not a code change.

members.concern: Asks for brief comments on the device_thread routine of the new t_clearhbm test (what it does, how it works) and for documentation of the TRON_POISON_BITS environment variable the test reads.

detection.trigger: A new function longer than about 20 lines, or a new environment-variable read (getenv), lands with no comment above it.
detection.procedure: For each new function in the diff, count comment lines inside and above it; grep the diff for getenv and check whether the variable name and its format are documented in a comment or a README.
detection.question: Could a reader of the file alone learn what the routine does and which environment variable controls it?

members.quote: I know this is a pretty simple routine, but I'm a fan of comments :). Can you add some brief comments about what this is doing/how, and how to use `TRON_POISON_BITS`?
members.note: Verified at d39c222fa8:t/t_clearhbm.cpp: device_thread at line 35 has no header comment; TRON_POISON_BITS is read at line 71 in main (outside the commented hunk), parsed with std::stoul(…, 0), default 0. Wade approved the same minute at the same commit; no reply in the digest. Self-labelled low severity ('pretty simple routine').

members.concern: Wade asks what 'erased' means in the new phrase 'four erased runtime binding classes', a specialist term (type erasure) used without definition in the spec.

detection.trigger: A doc, Note or comment hunk introduces an adjective or noun with a specialist meaning (type-theory, hardware, or project jargon) that the document does not define and that a general dictionary does not give in that sense.
detection.procedure: List every new technical term in the added prose. For each, grep the full document (and its glossary section) for a definition before the use site. If none, ask for a gloss at first use.
detection.question: Does the document define this term before or at this use?

members.note: Shortest comment in the corpus: a single quoted word with a question mark. Author glossed it in 3b1f9ae: exact semantic types are erased to four storage classes at this level; exact-type evidence belongs to the producer/admission layer. Wade needed the full document to know the term had no glossary entry (section 2 glossary exists in the file).

members.concern: The spec introduces the term 'safe mode' (the interpreter validating a full program set before writing to hardware) for the first time with no definition and no link to where it is described or how it is selected.

detection.trigger: An added prose line uses a quoted or capitalised mode/feature name (here 'safe mode') that does not appear elsewhere in the file before this line and has no link, footnote or parenthetical definition.
detection.procedure: For each distinctive term in added documentation lines, grep the file at HEAD for earlier occurrences and for a link target; grep the rest of the docs tree and the referenced code repositories for a section that defines it. If the first occurrence is in the diff and no pointer exists, ask for a definition or a link, naming what a reader needs (how it is enabled, disabled, chosen).
detection.question: Is this the term's first appearance, and does the text give the reader a definition or a pointer to where the mechanism is described?

members.quote: first mention of 'safe mode'... is there a link/reference pointer to where this is better described (e.g. how it's enabled/disabled/dictated/driven)?
members.note: Author addressed it in e7c2c00 a month later: safe mode was a per-call-site entry-point choice (execute vs execute_trusted vs prepare_trusted+execute_prepared) documented in asimov-interpreter src/README.md; the caption now says so, and the author flagged that the 2026-08-26 interpreter rewrite collapsed the modes. Wade approved three minutes after asking, so the question did not gate approval. Same reader-first instinct as the plain-English 'define a term at first use' rule.

members.concern: Wade prefers the default argument values (rx_xfer = false, readback_offset = 0xffffffff) to appear at the function definition as well as at the declaration, as documentation; the author points out C++ forbids re-stating a default at the definition.

detection.trigger: A hunk removes a default value from a function definition's parameter list ('bool rx_xfer = false' -> 'bool rx_xfer') because the default moved to a header declaration, or adds a new defaulted parameter whose default is visible only in the header.
detection.procedure: grep the header for the declaration (grep -n 'xfer_blocks' h/libpos.hpp) and confirm the defaults live there. The C++ rule (a default argument may be specified only once per scope) means the definition cannot repeat them; the only possible remedy is a comment at the definition naming the defaults. Report as a comment ask, never as a code change.
detection.question: Are the defaults visible to a reader of the definition, by a comment, given that the language forbids repeating them?

members.quote: kinda pedantic, but I like to see the default parameter values replicated in the implementation too (rx_xfer, readback_offset)... just helps enhance 'documentation' of the code
members.note: Declaration at head: h/libpos.hpp line 286 'uint32_t readback_offset = 0xffffffff) noexcept;'. The definition's doc comment (driver.cpp line 703) already says '@param readback_offset OPTIONAL, defaults to 0xffffffff'. Wade's ask is not implementable as code; the author offered a comment. Self-labelled 'kinda pedantic' = nit.

members.concern: When the spec demotes the older Haskell model and GOLD_V1 encoding doc to 'no longer the stated authority' while leaving them in place, Wade asks what the plan is to retire them and the two branch-only draft specs that early adopters were told to read, so newcomers do not find several competing specs.

detection.trigger: A doc hunk says an existing document or artifact 'is no longer the authority', 'remains but', 'superseded', 'deprecated' or 'legacy' and does not delete it or turn it into a pointer.
detection.procedure: grep the diff for 'no longer', 'superseded', 'deprecated', 'legacy', 'older', 'remain'. For each demoted document, list where it lives (repo path, other repo, unmerged branch: gh api repos/<org>/<repo>/branches and open PRs touching the same topic). Check the PR body and the document's status/roadmap section for a sentence that says when and how each demoted document is removed or replaced by a pointer. If none, ask for the retirement plan.
detection.question: Does the text say when and how each superseded document goes away, and who owns that step?

members.quote: what is our retirement plan for these older docs? It's confusing (esp. for newer folks) to come across multiple specs in multiple locations, and then add to that the in-flight / uncommitted docs in branches of this repo
members.note: Wade cited two branch URLs of the same repo (bgamari-gold-spec and add-gold-doc) that hold draft specs not on any merge path; that fact is discoverable from the repo's branches, but the claim that 'early adopters were told to reference' them is team knowledge. Author added a section 16 'Docs' row with the retirement plan in 3b1f9ae (tombstone pointer pattern, close PR #34, delete branches). Digest header shows commit 3b1f9ae87b for this comment though the review was at c57b748.

codex_bullets.bullet: Separate model dimensions from hardware storage dimensions. Trace bounds, padding, alignment, and unsupported-model fallback through the production caller. Do not infer production behavior from a test-only helper.
codex_bullets.reason: Five comments (PRs 4007, 2176, 2233); also 3002034511 and 3283298134. Recurring theme in the hardware-attention code. No Claude check.

codex_bullets.bullet: Hardware geometry: trace dimensions from model configuration through hardware eligibility, packing, transfer construction, and consumption. Keep the model's logical shape separate from the hardware's stored shape. Check padding and alignment against the instructions actually used.
codex_bullets.reason: Five comments (PRs 4007, 2176, 4128, 2148). Procedure form of C6; adopt together.

codex_bullets.bullet: Compare singleton, batched, partial, and fallback routes that the change affects. Distinguish a production route from a test utility or an inactive debug file. Recheck current hardware and build constraints instead of assuming those in an old review still hold.
codex_bullets.reason: Three Wade comments (PRs 4007, 4128) plus the 4128 paste. The production-vs-test-utility distinction (4007, two comments) is worth one sentence.
